title: Congressman Pat Harrigan votes for bill to address safety in Washington, D.C. - Hickory Sun
text:
Congressman Pat Harrigan of North Carolina’s 10th District voted on Mar. 25 in favor of H.R. 5103, known as the Make the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Act of 2026. The legislation aims to restore order, improve public safety, and protect the nation’s capital from vandalism and crime.
The issue is important because Washington, D.C. serves as a symbol for visitors from across the country and around the world. According to Harrigan, “Washington, D.C. is the front door of our country, and right now it is not living up to that standard.” He added that people should be able to visit monuments and walk city streets with pride but said disorder and weak enforcement have become problems.
Harrigan said, “Instead, we have allowed disorder, vandalism, and weak enforcement to take hold. That is not acceptable. This bill is about restoring basic standards, backing up our law enforcement, and making sure our nation’s capital reflects the strength and character of the American people.” The act would codify an executive action by former President Trump focused on cleaning graffiti and repairing monuments while creating a federal commission to coordinate safety efforts across agencies in Washington.
The legislation also addresses what supporters describe as ongoing public safety failures by challenging sanctuary-style policies in the district and calling for a stronger law enforcement presence.
Harrigan has been active in legislative matters since his election victory over Ralph R. Scott Jr., winning with 57.5% of votes compared to Scott’s 38.2%, according to [election results].
Harrigan urged senators to pass this measure so that Washington can better reflect what he called “the strength, order, and values of the American people.”
